newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-KUERTEN MAKES QUICK EXIT ON GRASS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KUERTEN MAKES QUICK EXIT ON GRASS.

text.p: French Open champion Gustavo Kuerten suffered a discouraging start to his grass court career on Tuesday, crashing out of the pre-Wimbledon Nottingham men's tournament 6-1 7-5 to big-serving Briton Greg Rusedski.

Kuerten, who took Paris by storm with his unseeded final victory over former champion Sergi Bruguera, could not get to grips with the slippery surface and won only three points against Rusedski's serve in the 18-minute first set.

But he rallied in the second; earning a couple of break points. He said afterwards he had a lot to learn about playing on grass. The 20-year-old Brazilian, third seed here, is seeded 11th at Wimbledon which starts next week.

Eighth seed Todd Woodbridge of Australia also fell at the first hurdle losing 6-2 2-6 6-2 to Zimbabwe's Byron Black, but his Wimbledon doubles partner Mark Woodforde beat Jonathan Stark and sixth seed Jim Courier beat Johan van Herck 6-3 3-6 6-3.
